root_cause.text: In `mlx5e_ipsec_disable_events()` the mlx5 driver unconditionally dereferenced the peer’s `ipsec` pointer after only checking `peer_priv`, so switchdev-mode teardown on devices without IPsec support hit a NULL pointer dereference during IPsec resource cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The crash trace shows the fault in `mlx5e_ipsec_disable_events+0xb6` at `complete_all(&peer_priv->ipsec->comp)`, and the patch changes the guard from `if (peer_priv)` to `if (peer_priv && peer_priv->ipsec)`, matching the commit message that “when the device doesn't support IPsec, we try to clean up the IPsec resources anyway.”

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is the new helper `mlx5e_ipsec_disable_events()`, not the old buggy teardown path. It explicitly avoids operating when there is no devcom: `if (!priv->devcom) return;`. It then iterates peers and only dereferences peer IPsec state in the controlled context `if (peer_priv) complete_all(&peer_priv->ipsec->comp);`, which is part of the cleanup ordering fix. The root-cause bug was an unconditional dereference of the peer's `ipsec` pointer after only checking `peer_priv`; that vulnerable construct is not present here. The commit also adds the safety check in `mlx5e_ipsec_send_event()`: `if (!priv->ipsec || mlx5_devcom_comp_get_size(priv->devcom) < 2) return;`, which shows the fix is already present in this version.
